claim: The fixed-horizon renewal type code is a proper full-support block distribution with uniform pointwise regret O(sqrt(N)) over every stationary binary renewal law with arbitrary finite mean.
quantifiers: All N>=1 and all positive-integer gap distributions of finite mean, with no uniform mean or tail bound.
proof: RESULT.txt Section1: type size (N-S)R!/product C!; separate allzero type; regeneration bounds true probability by product gap masses; multinomial probability is <=1; partition generating product gives log K_N<=log2+2sqrt(2N).
inputs: Explicit binary string and horizon. No gap law or partition-count oracle supplied; integer partitions are computed.
costs: O(N^2) integer additions for K_N, polynomial-size type statistics. The definition enumerates no types in its implementation.
baseline: Renewal type compression and HJW established O(sqrt N) redundancy; candidate novelty is computational marginalization, not the redundancy rate.
falsifier: Incorrect type fibres, a missing stationary boundary factor, or a renewal law violating the multinomial domination.
unresolved_gate: External proof review and detailed prior enumerative-code comparison.

claim: Every ordered prefix marginal of the fixed Q_N is computed exactly by a two-table weighted integer partition DP.
quantifiers: All binary prefixes of lengths 0<=t<=N; one-based anchors; positive interarrival distances; complete-gap count r; next gap strictly greater than terminal zero age b.
proof: RESULT.txt Sections2-3: random multiset permutations give product falling factorials/(R)_r; the terminal survival statistic is an additive marked residual count. Separate R=r and allzero-prefix branches. DP enumerates local multiplicities, not exponential suffixes.
inputs: Observed prefix only; same fixed horizon for all calls.
costs: Conservative O(N^4) integer operations and O(N^2) states per marginal; integer table bit length O(N log N).
baseline: Exponential brute type/string enumeration used only for finite validation; no NML optimization oracle.
falsifier: Replacing j>b by j>=b, dropping S<=N-a, or dividing by R-r when R=r.
unresolved_gate: Independent external/formal validation; faster exponents are not required for this proof.

claim: Every grouped prefix denominator divides N!, so H_N(y)=K_N N! Q_N(y) is an exactly computable nonnegative integer.
quantifiers: All feasible type states 0<=R<=S<=N-1, R>=r; R>r denominator is (N-S)(R)_{r+1} and R=r denominator is (N-S)R!.
proof: N-S<=N-R, hence N-S divides (N-R)! and (N-S)R! divides N!=binom(N,R)(N-R)!R!. Falling factorial denominators divide R!. Allzero-prefix denominators N-S divide N!.
inputs: Same explicit horizon/prefix; factorials computed locally.
costs: H_N(y)<=K_N N!, O(N log N) bits. Exact average of n ratios may require O(N^2 log N) output bits and is separately charged.
baseline: Root's safe factorial-power common denominator remains valid; this stronger integer scaling avoids rational accumulation per marginal.
falsifier: A feasible state denominator not dividing N! or prefix normalization failing under integer scaling.

claim: Averaging suffix conditionals of the fixed horizon N=n+1 yields a polynomial-bit-time terminal predictor with uniform expected KL O(n^-1/2).
quantifiers: Every n>=1, every binary input path, and the entire stationary finite-mean renewal class without a uniform mean bound.
proof: RESULT.txt Section4 reconstructs convexity, stationarity, KL chain rule, and memory DPI. The latter is bounded by I(Z1;X^N)=I(min(Z1,N+1);X^N)<=log(N+1), so even infinite H(Z1) creates no missing premise.
inputs: One trajectory. No gap law, mixing margin, resets, or conditional probability oracle.
costs: O(n) marginal calls; conservative O(n^7 log^2(n+2)) bit time and polynomial space. Exact rational average is charged.
baseline: HJW Proposition1 supplies the established statistical conversion; its Theorem4 supplies matching statistical lower order. This candidate only changes the computational implementation of a valid block code.
falsifier: A hidden mean-bound dependence, horizon switching invalidating the KL telescope, or a nonfinite information manipulation requiring H(Z1)<infinity.
unresolved_gate: External proof/formal validation and later primary-literature comparison. Expected terminal risk is not worst-context or high-probability accuracy.
